reason: Prioritize int3-g64 as the clearest quality-safe memory hypothesis: 3-bit g128 used 1,819 MiB but retained only 0.80 quality, so smaller groups may improve quantization quality while retaining a likely memory advantage over 4-bit. Second, mixed3-4-g64 tests finer grouping on the only mixed recipe with measured quality near the gate (0.85 at g128). Neither is proven to meet both retention gates: BF16 throughput is absent, no heldout tasks were measured, and smaller groups may add overhead. The board's vdown4-rest3 hypothesis is next because it targets sensitive modules, but the supplied data gives no direct evidence it restores quality. int4 has the strongest observed quality evidence, yet its 2,299 MiB peak offers less memory reduction; mixed2-4's fast sample had zero quality. Treat rankings as hypotheses, not results.
